task: Turn Reality Architect into an assessment-to-artifact open-method product with a truthful implementation and privacy boundary.
surface: Homepage, assessment, architecture brief export, implementation options, metadata, public/private boundary, and local-data privacy route.
audience: Creators, founders, and operators moving from repeated AI use toward dependable workflow architecture.
first_read: Find the system gap. Build the next artifact.

references.label: Reality Architect public method
references.reason: Preserves the five dependent moves and open-source contract.

references.label: Private Vault boundary
references.reason: Informed the boundary without copying private systems, evidence, or paid material.

references.label: Premium Web OS
references.reason: Required a working proof object, named motion, reduced-motion behavior, and honest release evidence.

avoid: Unsupported life, income, or transformation claims
Private Vault material in public artifacts
direction.signature: The assessment resolves one dependency gap into an exportable architecture brief with an acceptance test and guardrail.

asset_quality.why_premium: The primary proof is the actual assessment and architecture artifact rather than decorative media or conceptual product claims.

artifacts.notes: Local assessment, first-gap and completed-loop logic, Markdown artifact, deferred download cleanup, copy, browser-state privacy, focused result state, and accessibility semantics reviewed in source and compiled.
First viewport now shows an exact artifact preview and literal product promise.
The public method now matches the five-move workflow contract and explicitly excludes diagnostic, health, personality, financial-potential, and future-outcome claims.
Open method, planned digital product, scoped guided service, and private boundary are explicit.

Desktop, 390px mobile, and reduced-motion renders inspected. The route distinguishes local assessment state and user-triggered exports from ordinary hosting request logs without claiming zero infrastructure logging.

System Chrome and Playwright inspected the existing production build at 1440px desktop, 390px mobile, 640 CSS px reflow, keyboard focus, and prefers-reduced-motion. Assessment gap and completed-loop results, Markdown download, clipboard parity after line-ending normalization, Start/Vault handoff, canonicals, storage, requests, and runtime errors passed. Temporary captures and qa-report.json live outside the tracked tree under %TEMP%/realityarchitect-visual-qa-20260710.

checks.name: asset-tier
checks.evidence: Tier C is the correct medium: the primary proof is the functional, code-authored assessment and privacy interface rather than decorative media. No new generated or external asset was introduced.

checks.name: export-inspection
checks.evidence: Actual full-page desktop, 390px mobile, and reduced-motion privacy renders plus the completed mobile assessment result were inspected from the production build; composition, hierarchy, overflow, and trust copy passed.

checks.name: frozen-install
checks.evidence: pnpm 11.5.0 frozen install passes; postcss is overridden to 8.5.15 and the prior medium advisory is resolved.

checks.name: lint-and-type
checks.evidence: pnpm lint and pnpm typecheck pass.

checks.name: claims
checks.evidence: Public claims scan passes across 19 app, component, library, public, and README sources, including explicit regression blockers for the removed health/science overclaims.

checks.name: tests
checks.evidence: Eight product-contract tests pass for Markdown export reliability, sensitive assessment fields having no network/persistence/telemetry sink, the public privacy boundary, completed-loop review logic, no fake email capture, paid-offer readiness, method claims boundaries, and canonical metadata.

checks.name: build
checks.evidence: Next.js 16.2.7 production build compiled and prerendered 13 static routes, including /privacy.

checks.name: security
checks.evidence: Untrusted-repo intake, source secret scan, frozen dependency audit, and changed-file private-memory marker review pass. The only marker hits are intentional source words such as client component, secrets guardrail, and private-input boundary; no personal or premium Vault content is present.

checks.name: metadata
checks.evidence: Generated HTML has exact canonical and Open Graph URLs for home, method, standard, assess, start, Vault, and privacy; the sitemap includes all seven public routes. The privacy route is intentionally index/follow.

checks.name: visual-qa
checks.evidence: The production build was inspected at 1440px desktop and 390px mobile, including reduced motion: /privacy returns 200 with its exact canonical, index/follow policy, visible navigation/footer access, no overflow, and no console errors. A completed assessment kept private fixture values in the in-page brief, wrote no storage or cookies, and emitted only bodyless same-origin Next.js prefetch GETs.

score.notes: The proof-led assessment has a literal first read, product-specific blueprint identity, strong typography and spacing, intentional mobile composition, visible focus, static reduced-motion behavior, truthful offer boundaries, valid exports, and no runtime artifacts. It is ready for human review; the protected Git preview still requires normal Vercel access.

known_risks: The Git preview is Vercel-auth protected; direct browser inspection used the same head production build locally and production remains unchanged.
The digital product is intentionally not purchasable until delivery and commercial terms are complete.
Guided review availability is not guaranteed and must be scoped before payment.

Analytics for assessment completion and export are not added until consent and data-governance choices are made; any future measurement must exclude answers, system names, repeating jobs, and brief text.
